desc: Understand the parity invariant: paired elements must have indices of opposite parity (distance odd). This restricts the matching to pair each even-indexed element with an odd-indexed element, leaving at most one odd unpaired.

Derive a correct algorithm: Use a stack to simulate optimal non-crossing pairings while maximizing sum of |A_i - A_j|. Process elements left to right, maintaining a deque or stack of unmatched elements of the majority parity. At each step, decide whether to pair the current element with the top of the stack or push it.

Implement the stack-based greedy: For each element, if stack is non-empty and top has opposite parity, compute the score of pairing them; otherwise, push the current element. Keep track of the maximum total score achievable. This must be O(N) or O(N log N).
Test the solution with the provided sample inputs to ensure correctness.
Consider edge cases such as N=2, N=3, and arrays with duplicate values.
Ensure 64-bit integer handling for sums up to ~3e14.
